tasks.title: Lock Lifecycle Kernel Contracts
tasks.description: Four focused policy tests encode the single kernel authority, intake obligations, delivery and verification obligations, and optional non-cyclic workflow, and fail against the current unmodified surfaces for the intended missing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: One test requires the lifecycle skill to contain the sole named Contract–Seam–Feedback definition and compact rule.
One test requires init, research, and create to carry their bounded intake and decision obligations without naming CSF.
One test requires ship and verify to carry thin-slice, consequence-based evidence, conditional MVP, and feedback-routing obligations without naming CSF.
One test requires the generic lifecycle workflow to be optional and non-cyclic.
Existing planning-boundary and Hindsight lifecycle contracts remain green.
No production prompt, skill, workflow, or template is modified by this task.

node --experimental-strip-types --test --test-name-pattern="planning boundaries and testability contract is conditional|parent lifecycle memory policy uses Hindsight" .pi/tests/skill-system.test.ts
tasks.expected_verification_state: The new named contracts fail only because the lifecycle obligations are absent; the existing baseline tests pass.

tasks.title: Establish the Lifecycle Kernel and Optional Workflow
tasks.description: The lifecycle skill becomes the single named authority for contract, justified seams, evidence depth, artifact mapping, and feedback routes, while the generic workflow is explicitly optional and non-cyclic.
acceptance_criteria: The lifecycle skill contains one concise Contract–Seam–Feedback definition and compact enforcement rule.
The lifecycle skill maps contract, seam decisions, task authority, attempt evidence, and durable learning to the existing artifacts and Hindsight.
The lifecycle skill routes unknown facts, changed desired behavior, architecture or design gaps, and known implementation defects to the correct earliest phase.
Route selection never automatically invokes a command, mutates .active, or changes lifecycle state.
The generic lifecycle workflow is described as an optional bounded helper rather than the canonical lifecycle or a mandatory research-to-verification cycle.
The workflow does not repeat the CSF name, acronym, or full doctrine.

tasks.title: Align Intake and Decision Phases
tasks.description: Initialization, research, and specification creation each emit their bounded decision input, observable contract, risk controls, and conditional product or release learning signal without duplicating the named kernel.
acceptance_criteria: Init identifies validated intended outcomes, major external, trust, and volatility boundaries, and available evidence channels when relevant, without inventing speculative seams.
Research records the decision question, evidence, confidence, alternatives, contract impact, and unresolved risks and remains on demand.
Create requires essential journeys, inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, non-goals, and non-deferrable risk controls in observable success behavior.
Create requires a measurable learning signal or real feedback path only for product or release-level specifications.
None of the three prompts contains the CSF acronym or repeats the named kernel.

tasks.title: Align Delivery, Verification, and Feedback
tasks.description: Shipping and verification favor observable thin slices, deepen evidence for the approved consequence set, distinguish product learning from technical readiness, and route findings without automatic phase transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Ship directs behavioral work toward the smallest safe end-to-end slice and a failing observable boundary test first where practical.
Ship does not require speculative interfaces, private-method mocks, or test-only production APIs.

Verify retains changed-file mode selection but independently escalates for security, privacy, authorization or tenant isolation, data integrity, external providers, retries or idempotency, cost controls, and recovery.
Verify starts with essential observable journeys and controlled failures, records evidence vantage, and requires a named evidence gap for deeper checks.
Product or release MVP readiness requires a learning signal or feedback path and cannot be equated with internal tests or reviewer score.
Feedback routes to research, create, plan, or ship without automatic command execution, .active mutation, or phase cycling.
Neither prompt contains the CSF acronym or repeats the named kernel.

tasks.title: Verify Integrated Lifecycle Behavior
tasks.description: All lifecycle contracts, retained tests, graph validation, artifact authority, Hindsight policy, and untouched planning surfaces pass together with no out-of-scope changes.
acceptance_criteria: All focused lifecycle contract tests pass with zero failures.
The complete retained test suite passes with zero failures.
Every artifact task graph validates.
Cross-artifact frontier reporting leaves .active byte-identical.
The plan prompt, planning skill, PRD template, and task-graph implementation remain unchanged.
Only declared implementation and lifecycle evidence paths are owned by this feature; runtime-managed and unrelated state remains untouched.
An independent read-only review has no unresolved critical or important findings.
